Worked example: a weak and a strong analysis (metaphor)

The same device and the same sentence beginnings. Only the ideas after the beginnings make the difference.

✗ Weak

Collins states, “all the dark blue speed drained out of it.” The verb “drained” is significant because it is an interesting word. Collins compares speed to a liquid to suggest something about the poem. He also emphasizes feelings. The reader is sad because it is sad. They also realize it is important. Through the use of a metaphor, Collins presents things about life.

  • The word is not explained: “a good word” could be said about any word.
  • “Something about the poem” and “feelings” could fit any poem.
  • “Sad because it is sad” gives no reason from the words, and “life” is not a message.
✓ Strong

Collins states, “all the dark blue speed drained out of it.” The verb “drained” is significant because it suggests the excitement of childhood is slowly flowing away. Collins compares the bicycle's speed to a liquid that has drained away to suggest that the speaker has lost the energy and excitement of early childhood. He also emphasizes how lifeless ordinary objects now seem. The reader is saddened because the once-exciting bicycle now seems lifeless. They also realize that the change is inside the speaker, not the bike. Through the use of a metaphor, Collins presents the loss of the excitement and energy of early childhood.

  • Step 4 explains what the word suggests in THIS poem.
  • The device frame says exactly what the device shows in this poem.
  • The feeling has a reason that comes from the words, and the link gives a clear message.
The introduction (in the exam, it is given)

① Choose 2 devices that directly connect to the thesis in the introduction. Choose smartly.
  • The thesis is the last sentence: growing up means losing the magic and innocence of childhood and discovering that life can hurt.
  • A strong pair: one device about the magic of early childhood and one about the sadness of growing up.

Reminders
  • Collins is a man: write he or Collins, never “she.”
  • Copy quotations exactly and put them inside quotation marks.
  • In step 4, zoom in on ONE word and name its word class first: “The adjective “___” is …” or “The noun “___” is …”.
  • Each box gets a gold star when every part of its structure is there. The ticks check structure; the 💡 hints help with ideas.
Finish

    Exam practice · 40 minutes

    While you write: your paragraph score (out of 100) goes up live. Naming the device, copying exact words and explaining them count most. Coach messages appear in the bar at the top, so they never cover your writing. Read each one, then keep writing.

    The timer keeps running if you leave the page. When time is up, your paragraph is checked automatically.
